title: Reforj
description: An open world sandbox developed at 4J Studios
overview: I worked on reforj as part of the tools and engine team at 4J Studios. My main contributions to the project included developing and maintaining various tools and systems to support the game's development. This involved working closely with other teams to ensure that the tools met their needs and were easy to use. Additionally, I was responsible for implementing the backend for the UI system.

title: Isosurface Algorithms
overview: As part of my honours research, I created an application which allowed the user to edit voxel terrain using several techniques. The terrain was polygonised using isosurface techniques, including modified marching cubes and a dual contouring algorithm. In an effort to improve the efficiency, both the marching cubes algorithm and dual contouring algorithm were implemented on the GPU through the compute shader.

content.title: Marching Cubes

media.alt: A wireframe render of marching cubes terrain.

content.description: I implemented marching cubes on the compute shader adapting paul bourke's algorithm initially written on the CPU. For future, I aim to write an alternative algorithm which takes advantage of GPGPU techniques using a prefix scan to generate global indices and avoid using atomic increments to store triangles.

content.title: Dual Contouring

media.alt: A wireframe render of surface nets terrain.

content.description: I implemented Surface Nets on the compute shader based on some psuedo code aquired from a paper discussing the Isosurface algorithm.

title: Foundation Engine
description: An on going personal project exploring game engine development

media.alt: An image of the foundation engine editor.

overview: Foundation Engine is an ongoing personal project where I explore game engine development. The main focus of the project is to explore and research how systems are architected and the intercommunications between these systems.

content.title: Graphics
content.description: The foundation engine has seen a couple of rendering back-ends, from OpenGL 4.6 to DirectX 12. Currently, the rendering interface is implemented through NVRHI, Nvidia's abstracted rendering interface.

content.title: ENTT
content.description: Integrated into the world context (also referred to as the 'scene'), ENTT serves as the engine's main entity component system (ECS), enforcing a component based architecture. The world context owns and manages the entity registry, where entities are made accessible. Foundation also supports scriptable entities, allowing for custom behaviours and logic.

content.title: Services Registry
content.description: A debated topic in the game engine communicated, a services registry is implemented adhering to the service locator pattern, supporting global access to engine subsystems, like the file manager. An instance of the services registry is created in the core application and injected into each layer of the application. Long term, I'm aiming to refactor the service locator, and instead manage and expose subsystems within relevant contexts. For instance, the world context will own the AI Subsystem, which wil be made available to all scriptable entities. This approach should avoid global access and highlight dependencies.

title: Graphics Programming with Shaders (DX11)
description: Showcasing several graphics programming techniques in shaders

media.alt: A screenshot of the DX11 scene rendering several graphics techniques.

content.title: Vertex Manipulation
content.description: The application contains an ordinary plane which has it's vertices disstorted in the vertex shader from a height map. Additionally, a matrix of patches can be swapped into the scene demonstrating not only dynamic tessellation, see below, but also vertex displacement occurring in the domain shader.

content.title: Dynamic Tessellation
content.description: A GPU accelerated LOD surface patch algorithm was implemented across the hull shader and domain shader. A 12-point control patch was uploaded from the CPU where each patch was tessellated with respects to the camera's position. This enabled high resolution vertex displacement close to the camera while rendering less geometry further from the camera.

content.title: Gaussian Bloom
content.description: The chosen post processing techniqes were guassian bluring and box blurring. Post-processing takes place after the scene has been initially written to a render target. A mask is created from the render target and stored in a subsequent texture ready for the blur pass.

content.title: Shadow Mapping (PCF)
content.description: Shadow mapping was implemented for directional lighting and spotlights. Both hard shadows and soft shadows are supported. PCF was used as the method for soft shadows, supporting 3x3, 5x5 and 7x7 filtering.

content.title: Normal Mapping
content.description: The application supports normal mapping the extrapolation of world space normals from texture space by multiplying the coordinates by the TBN, Tangent, Bi-Tangent and Normal, matrix. Additionally, using partial derivatives, a per-vertex and per-pixel normal function was implemented. This enabled the generation of normals on the fly, adding significant amount of detail on lower resolution height-maps.

title: Procedural Generation (DX11)
description: Showcasing procedural generation techniques in DX11

media.alt: A screenshot of the DX11 scene rendering a height map and procedural waves.

overview: In the procedural methods module I implemented several procedural techniques on the CPU. The following techniques were implemented in a DX11 framework: Hydraulic Erosion, Trochoidial Waves, Voronoi Noise (GPU), Simplex Noise, Perlin Noise, Improved Perlin Noise, Octave Perlin Noise, Ridged Perlin Noise

content.title: Perlin Noise
content.description: Perlin Noise serves as the basis for most of the procedural techniques in this project. The perlin algorithm was implemented in C++ using the original C implemnetation as reference. Additionally, the improved perlin algorithm as well as the Simplex noise algorithms were implemented and can be used to drive the terrain generator.

content.title: Hydraulic Erosion
content.description: The Hydraulic erosion algorithm implemented aims to simulate the erosive features exerted on terrain from water droplets. Water droplets erode the terrain through bilinear interpolation across four vertices taking into account the gradient at each point. If the droplet identifies the current cell is a pit, the droplet releases sediment until the pit has been filled.

content.title: Trochoidial Waves
content.description: Trochoidial waves were implemented on the vertex shader and textured using a voronoi noise pattern, discussed below. The algorithm aims to capture the motion of waves by displacing the vertices using sine and cosine operations. To procure the sharp troughs, an offset with respect to the original vertex position, the anchor point, is applied in both the 'x' and 'z' directions to produce circular motion. The amplitude is controlled through a ratio, s / k, where 's' is a value between '0' and '1' and 'k' is 2 * PI divided by the wavelength.

title: Animation Systems
description: A 2D and 3D animation system imlpemented in C++
overview: In the Animation Systems module, I implemented the following systems and animation techniques Entity Component System, Blend Tree (3D Animation), 2D Armature Json Parser, 2D Skeleton Animator, Sprite Json Parser, Sprite Animator

content.title: 2D Sprite Animation
content.description: An armature parser was implemented capable of reading and extrapolating armature data from a Json file format. The parser reads from a file containing all the necessary data to perform 2D skeletal animation, such as bones, skin and frame data, then stores the data into components.

content.title: 3D Animation
content.description: A 3D skeletal animation system was implemented supporting keyframe interpolation and animation blending. The animation system is integrated into an entity component system architecture, allowing for flexible and modular animation management. A blend tree system was also developed to facilitate smooth transitions between different animation states based on user-defined parameters.

content.title: Blend Tree
content.description: A blend tree was implemented allowing the user to construct complex animation states with minimum code. The tree supports the following nodes: Animation Clip, Linear Blend, 2D Blend, Additive Blend, Ragdoll, Output. Additionally, the blend tree supports multiple data attributes, controlling different aspects of the animations.

title: Up For Delivery
description: A 3D puzzle game developed in Unreal Engine 4
overview: In the summer of 2022, I worked as part of a team to develop a 3D puzzle game in Unreal Engine 4. The game, Up For Delivery (UFD), is a single-player experience where the player must navigate through a series of increasingly difficult levels by solving puzzles and overcoming obstacles. My main contributions to the project included level design, scripting gameplay mechanics using Blueprints, and implementing materials.

content.title: Project Management
content.description: Utilized project management tools such as Jira to facilitate effective communication and task tracking within the team. This ensured that all team members were aligned on project goals and deadlines.

content.title: Materials and Scripting
content.description: Implemented various materials to enhance the visual appeal of the game environment. Additionally, scripted gameplay mechanics using Unreal Engine's Blueprint system to create interactive elements and ensure a cohesive gaming experience.

title: Networking
description: A networking project developed during my studies
overview: During my studies, I undertook a networking project where I developed a multiplayer networking system for a game. The system was designed to handle real-time communication between clients and the server, ensuring smooth gameplay experiences even under varying network conditions.

content.title: Boids Algorithm
content.description: A boids based flocking system was implemented to simulate the collective behavior of autonomous agents. The algorithm incorporates three primary rules: separation, alignment, and cohesion, allowing the agents to navigate the environment while avoiding collisions and maintaining group dynamics.

content.title: Prediction and Interpolation
content.description: To ensure smooth and responsive movement of networked entities, prediction and interpolation techniques were employed. Prediction allows clients to estimate the future position of entities based on their current state, while interpolation smooths out the movement by calculating intermediate positions between received updates.

content.title: Testing and Optimization
content.description: Using tools to simulate various network conditions, the networking system was rigorously tested to identify and address latency, packet loss, and jitter issues. Optimization strategies were implemented to enhance performance and ensure a seamless multiplayer experience.

title: AI
description: An AI project developed during my studies
overview: The primary aim of the project was to successfully train agents to complete a simple race track. Each agent is rewarded for traveling the furthest from spawn as well as receiving bonuses for reaching checkpoints without crashing. Each agent contains a neural network. The neural networks are composed of several layers of weights. Initially, the weights are randomised and with each successive generation, successful agents lend their networks to the next generation. In an effort to reflect real world behaviours, each generation is subjected to a trace amount of mutation, which involves slightly modifying the agents weights.

content.title: Neural Networks
content.description: A feedforward neural network was implemented to enable agents to learn and adapt to their environment. The network consists of an input layer, one or more hidden layers, and an output layer. The agents were trained using supervised learning techniques, allowing them to make decisions based on the data they received from their surroundings.
